messages:
incident-bot: SEV2: Multiple ELB 502/503 errors observed serving model endpoints in eu-central-1b. Auto-triggered when error rate > 4% across frontends. Pager routed to #incidents and @sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: I'm on it. seeing elevated 5xx across two load balancer target groups for model-serving-prod-euc1b.

maria: Confirmed. CloudWatch shows spike in TargetResponseTime and Increased 504s from some backend instances. Route53 health checks are also failing for a subset of endpoints.

raj: I can start digging into ENI/instance metrics. Any recent deploys?

eng-runtime: No deploys in the last 2 hours. Autoscaling did not fire; target counts steady. Kernel logs show `conntrack` churn on a few instances earlier.

netops-lead: Route53 traces show elevated latency from eu-central-1 DNS resolver to the ELB A records for the problematic AZ. Could be local AZ networking or ELB control plane anomalies.

prod-support: Customer reports coming in: two customers in EU complaining of 502s for chat and embeddings. CS triage tagging accounts and telling customers we're investigating.

sre-oncall: Starting triage checklist: 1) Identify unhealthy targets 2) Confirm if ENI saturation or EBS IO are contributing 3) Reroute traffic if AZ is degraded.

eng-runtime: Running `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <TG-ARN>` now. Output: 3/8 targets Unhealthy (connection-reset / 502).

raj: Pulling instance-level metrics. I see high network packet drops on eni-0a12... & elevated `tcptrack` retransmits. CPU fine, memory fine.

maria: Route53 health checks failing from multiple locations for the ELB CNAME in eu-central-1b. But eu-central-1a/1c health checks are green.

netops-lead: Hypothesis: AZ-specific network fabric flapping causing ELB to drain/backplane issues. Plan: shift weighted Route53 records away from eu-central-1b to eu-central-1a/c as immediate mitigation.

eng-runtime: +1 for weight shift. Prepare a staged weight change: 0% -> 10% -> 0% for euc1b.

sre-oncall: Maria, can you run the weighted change? Also prepare rollback steps.

maria: On it. Will update Route53 traffic policy. Command snippet:

```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZABCDEFGHI --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet": {"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"euc1a","Weight":50,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.0.1.1"}]}}]}'
```

prod-support: Notifying customers that we're performing traffic shift to restore availability.

incident-bot: Action scheduled: route53-weighted-change by maria in 60s.

maria: applied change -> shifted 65% traffic to euc1a/c, 35% left on euc1b for canary. Monitoring.

eng-runtime: Metrics: error rate across frontends dropped from 6.2% -> 1.1% over next 90s. Latency improved. Looks promising.

raj: Verified network errors on problematic instances persist. I'm preparing to drain and replace 3 targets that repeatedly fail health checks.

sre-oncall: Please do replacement. Use lifecycle: deregister target -> wait for 30s -> terminate and let ASG replace.

raj: Deregistered targets tg-12345: eni-0a12..., eni-0b34..., eni-0c56...; terminating instances i-0aa111, i-0bb222, i-0cc333 now.

eng-runtime: Adding connection logging to ELB for 15m to capture patterns.

netops-lead: Meanwhile, I'm opening AWS support case: suspected AZ networking fabric issue impacting ENI routing in eu-central-1b. Case ID: 1234567890.

prod-support: CS updated major affected customers: we ran a targeted traffic shift and instance replacements. Asking for additional context if they need mitigation.

maria: After instance replacement, target health stabilized to 8/8 healthy in the group. Error rate holding ~0.9%.

incident-bot: Reminder: SEV2 escalation timer at 25m.

sre-oncall: Keeping incident open for monitoring and AWS follow-up. We'll hold weighted shift until AWS confirms root cause. Keeping 35% traffic in euc1b for now but routing can be toggled.

eng-runtime: Captured ELB logs show repeated `502` accompanied by `connection reset by peer` from the backend IPs tied to the ENIs we terminated. Suggests packet drops on host link.

raj: AWS responded: They see packet loss on hypervisor networking for a subset of hosts in eu-central-1b. They're evacuating impacted hosts. We requested SLA impact and a sticky mitigation (shifting traffic) while they remediate.

sre-oncall: Good. Next actions: 1) Keep traffic shifted to euc1a/c 2) Continue draining suspect targets 3) Keep customers informed 4) Schedule incident bridge for postmortem.

prod-support: Logging support tickets and CS notes; set expectation for a follow-up within 2 hours.

maria: Rolling euc1b weight to 10% now for canary (we have green targets). Watching for any error spike.

eng-runtime: No spike observed for 10m. Safe to continue reducing euc1b to 0% if AWS confirms full remediation.

netops-lead: AWS says their control plane changes finished, hosts are being drained, but they recommend leaving traffic off the AZ for 30 more minutes.

sre-oncall: Agreed. We'll keep euc1b at 0% for 30m. Setting follow-up reminder.

incident-bot: SEV2 -> Monitoring mode. Reminder: document timeline and capture logs for postmortem.

tom: I'll own the post-incident ticket. Will collect ELB logs, Route53 change history, ASG replacement events, and AWS case updates.

raj: Final note: we'll add an alert rule to detect AZ-specific ENI packet-drop spikes and tie it to oncall paging ASAP.

prod-support: All set. Communicating resolved status to impacted customers once AWS confirms.

sre-oncall: Summary: root cause likely AZ-level hypervisor networking packet loss causing backend resets -> ELB 502/503s. Mitigations: Route53 weighted shift, replace unhealthy instances, enable ELB logs. Postmortem + follow-ups assigned.

incident-bot: Incident will remain in this channel, mark resolved when the last_message_ts is updated.
